message.content:
When you toss three fair coins, the random variable \(X\) representing the number of heads follows a Binomial distribution with parameters \(n=3\) and success probability \(p=\tfrac12\).  
So the possible values of \(X\) are  

| Number of heads | Probability |
|-----------------|-------------|
| 0               | \(\binom{3}{0}(½)^0(½)^3 = \tfrac18\) |
| 1               | \(\binom{3}{1}(½)^1(½)^2 = \tfrac38\) |
| 2               | \(\binom{3}{2}(½)^2(½)^1 = \tfrac38\) |
| 3               | \(\binom{3}{3}(½)^3(½)^0 = \tfrac18\) |

In other words, you can obtain anywhere from **0 to 3 heads**; the most likely outcomes are getting one head or two heads (each with probability \(3/8\)).
